name: Theoretical computer science: Communication-minimizing DAG pebbling
description: Communication-minimizing DAG pebbling under a bounded candidate interface with independent verification; generated mathematical instances, no external dataset.

sources.locator: Hong and Kung: red-blue pebble game, dependency and transfer rules.

evaluation.benchmark: Theoretical computer science: Communication-minimizing DAG pebbling
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: pebble(dag, fast_memory_budget) -> list of [operation, vertex], with operations load/store/compute/delete. dag has topologically ordered parents and output vertices. Inputs start blue, all outputs must finish blue; every red value consumes one fast-memory slot, including newly computed results. Recomputations allowed; at most20000 operations. Score mean transfers / naive schedule on three layered DAGs; exact state-machine verification.

limitations: This is a bounded native adaptation, not the paper's experimental score or an asymptotic guarantee.
Public development generators can be inspected; independent generalization requires fresh instances after freezing the candidate.

papers.title: I/O Complexity: The Red-Blue Pebble Game
papers.task_relation: The local task constructs legal bounded-memory schedules for finite DAGs and counts loads and stores. Its instance family and verifier rules are a restricted scheduling adaptation and do not reproduce asymptotic bounds for matrix multiplication or FFT.
papers.primary_goal: Characterize and bound the input/output cost of computations with limited fast memory using pebble games.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Minimize data movement when evaluating a dependency graph with limited fast memory.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Communication cost under memory constraints is the explicit computational-complexity problem introduced by the source.
science_relevance.reason: The scientific target is communication-efficient computation itself, rather than incidental scoring of a planning agent.
